items.text: A new plan has been announced to build the UK’s first small modular reactors on the island of Anglesey. The project will take place at the former Wylfa nuclear station, which closed about ten years ago, and will bring major investment and up to 3,000 jobs. The first three reactors are expected to start operating by the mid-2030s and could supply enough energy for roughly three million homes. Local leaders believe this project will strengthen the island’s economy, which has suffered because of the closure of large industrial sites. They hope it will encourage young people to stay, work, and raise families on the island. Although many welcome the development, some residents remain sceptical . Opponents of nuclear power have raised concerns for decades and question whether the project truly represents progress for Anglesey. The government hopes that these SMRs will be quicker and cheaper to construct than traditional nuclear plants, helping the country increase clean energy production. Difficult words: sceptical (not fully believing something), opponent (a person who disagrees with something or tries to stop it). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The UK government plans to build new small modular reactors on the island of Anglesey. The work will start next year at the old Wylfa nuclear site, and the goal is to make energy by the mid-2030s. These reactors cost less, and building them is faster than normal nuclear plants. They can give power to about three million homes. The project can bring up to 3,000 jobs and help families stay in the area. Local leaders support the plan. They say the island needs new jobs because many young people leave to find work. Some people still worry; they question the safety and the future of the project. They want a clear plan that shows how the reactors can help the island in the long term . Difficult words: goal (what you want to achieve), safety (being protected and away from danger), long term (happening over a long period of time, not just now). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The UK government wants new small nuclear reactors on Anglesey. Workers start the job next year. The plan is to make power for three million homes in the 2030s. The reactors are small, fast to build, and not as expensive as big nuclear stations. People on the island hope for new jobs. Now, many young people leave the island for work. Officials say that the reactors can help families stay. The plan also brings money and new chances for the community . Some people do not like the idea. They worry about nuclear power. They want more information. They ask if the plan will really help Anglesey in the future. Difficult words: nuclear reactor (a machine which makes energy by breaking atoms), expensive (when something costs a lot of money), community (a group of people who live in the same place or share something important). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Scientists reported spectacular aurora borealis sightings across several US states and explained how these colorful displays are connected to powerful solar storms. These storms begin with huge eruptions of hot material and magnetic fields from the sun’s atmosphere. When they travel through space and reach Earth, they disturb our magnetic field and add large amounts of energy to it. This disturbance produces the northern and southern lights but also creates problems for modern technology. Solar storms accelerate charged particles toward Earth’s atmosphere, leading to strong electric currents in power networks. These events can also interfere with satellites. Controllers often work through the night to keep low-orbit satellites at the correct altitude, sometimes burning extra fuel to stop them from falling toward Earth. Other systems, such as rockets and GPS, also face difficulties. Precision GPS can become inaccurate by several centimeters during strong storms. Because of this, experts constantly communicate with infrastructure operators to reduce risks and protect vital technology. Difficult words: aurora borealis (colored lights in the sky near the North Pole), interfere (to cause difficulty for a system), precision (very exact accuracy). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Scientists see strong aurora borealis in many US states and explain that the lights come from solar storms. These storms start when the sun sends out hot material and magnetic energy. The storms move through space, reach Earth, and shake our magnetic field. This energy creates the northern and southern lights. The storms also cause trouble for power networks because they create electric currents . Satellites in low orbit face more drag , so controllers use extra fuel to keep them at the right height. Rockets and GPS also face problems. Very accurate GPS becomes less correct during strong storms. Because of this, experts talk all day with people who run important systems and try to keep everything safe. Difficult words: aurora borealis (colored lights in the sky near the North Pole), current (the flow of electricity in wires), drag (a force that pulls something back). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The sun is very hot and very active. It sends big storms into space. These storms move toward Earth. They shake Earth’s magnetic field and make strong energy. This makes the sky light up. People see the northern lights in many places. The storms also cause problems. Power lines get extra energy. Workers try to keep the system safe. Satellites in the sky need more fuel because the storms pull them down. GPS and rockets also have problems. GPS is not very correct in strong storms. Scientists look at the storms all the time and try to help people stay safe. Difficult words: shake (to move something quickly from side to side), magnetic field (a force around Earth or a magnet), power line (a long wire which brings electricity to homes and buildings). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

US President Donald Trump threatens the BBC with a billion-dollar lawsuit because his lawyers claim that a speech he gave before the 2021 Capitol riots was edited in a defamatory way. The BBC admitted to using misleading edits and apologized. As a result, the BBC’s Director General and News Chief resigned. The controversy also involves a leaked internal memo accusing the BBC of anti-Trump bias during the US election. Experts say Trump has a pattern of pressuring the media and using lawsuits to control his public image. Despite mistakes, the BBC argues it provides impartial news and remains a trusted broadcaster worldwide. Critics point out issues with impartiality in other controversial topics like Israel–Gaza reporting and debates about trans rights. The organization must maintain trust, represent diverse viewpoints, and defend independent media freedom while responding to legal and public pressures. The case highlights the tension between editorial choices, accountability , and freedom of expression in global media. Difficult words: defamatory (harming someone’s reputation with false information), impartiality (being fair and not taking sides), accountability (responsibility for actions). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Donald Trump threatens the BBC with a billion-dollar lawsuit . His lawyers say the BBC changed a speech he gave before the 2021 Capitol riots in the wrong way. The BBC says sorry and admits the edits. Because of this, the Director General and News Chief leave their jobs. A leaked memo says the BBC shows bias against Trump in the US election. Experts explain that Trump often pressures the media. The BBC says it gives fair news and wants people to trust it. People worry about other topics, like Israel–Gaza and trans rights. The BBC must show all points of view and protect free media while solving problems with the lawsuit. This event shows how the media can face pressure and stay responsible. Difficult words: lawsuit (a legal court case), admit (to say that something is true or that you did something), memo (a short written message or note used at work or in an organization), bias (unfair support for one side). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Donald Trump is angry with the BBC. He says the BBC changes his speech before the 2021 Capitol attack. He wants a big lawsuit . The BBC says sorry. The BBC also says that there are changes in Trump’s speech. BBC’s bosses leave their jobs. People say that the BBC does not always show both sides. Some experts say that Trump wants to control the news. The BBC wants to give fair news and keep people’s trust . People talk about other problems, like Israel and Gaza. The BBC must show all sides and keep the news free. This story shows that the news can make mistakes, but it must stay fair and honest for people. Difficult words: speech (a talk to people), lawsuit (a legal court case), trust (when someone believes you). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Levi’s plans to sell its 300-dollar Blue Tab jeans in more stores next year to meet the rising demand for premium denim. The line, launched earlier in Asia and in select stores in Europe and the US, features heavier Japanese selvedge denim, which is more durable and has self-finished edges. Compared to Levi’s traditional Red Tab jeans, which top out at 130 euros, Blue Tab cost up to 350 euros and jackets around 700 euros. While premium denim represents only about 10% of the 100-billion-dollar global denim market, it grows faster than standard jeans. Levi’s aims to attract more women and diversify its product range, including collaborations with brands like Nike and Barbour. Despite past challenges like inflation and US tariffs, the company expects a strong holiday season and plans to offer limited discounts. Levi’s may also acquire additional brands to accelerate growth, adding to its existing Beyond Yoga brand. Difficult words: premium (of high quality), selvedge (self-finished edge of cloth), acquire (to get or obtain something, often by buying or receiving it). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Levi’s will sell 300-dollar Blue Tab jeans in more stores next year because many people want expensive denim . The Blue Tab line started in Asia and some stores in Europe and the US. It uses strong Japanese denim that is thicker and lasts longer. Blue Tab jeans cost much more than regular Red Tab jeans, 130 euros compared to 300 euros. Jackets are also expensive; they can cost up to 700 euros. Premium jeans are a small part of the market but grow faster than other jeans. Levi’s wants to sell to more women and make more types of clothes. Collaborations with other brands like Nike help sales. The company expects good sales during the holidays and will give fewer discounts. Levi’s may buy other brands to grow faster. The plan also includes new designs for men and women next year. Difficult words: denim (a strong fabric used to make jeans and jackets), premium (of high quality), collaboration (working together). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Levi’s will sell 300-dollar Blue Tab jeans in more stores next year. The jeans are strong. They are from thick Japanese cloth. They cost more than normal Red Tab jeans. Red Tab jeans cost 130 euros, but Blue Tab jeans cost 300 euros. Levi’s wants more women to buy these jeans. The company will sell new jackets and clothes too. People like premium jeans. Levi’s thinks many will buy them. They work with other brands like Nike to sell more. Levi’s will give fewer sales and discounts . They also want to make new clothes for men and women. This plan helps Levi’s grow and sell more good products next year. Difficult words: thick (when there is a long distance between two sides), premium (of high quality), brand (a type of product which one company makes), discount (lower price). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

More than 130 gold and bronze artifacts have been returned to Ghana from the UK and South Africa. Many of them were taken from the Asante Kingdom during colonial times, while others were bought later on the open market. Some of the returned items were looted by British soldiers during the 1900 siege of Kumasi. The objects, including royal regalia , drums, and ceremonial gold weights, are between 45 and 160 years old and show the importance of gold in Asante culture. At a ceremony in Kumasi, King Otumfuo Osei Tutu II thanked the South African company AngloGold Ashanti and British art expert Hermione Waterfield for returning the pieces. Waterfield, a pioneering art historian, had long supported the restitution of African art. The event highlights Africa’s growing efforts to recover its cultural heritage and reconcile with colonial history. Difficult words: loot (to steal valuable things, especially during a war or after fighting), regalia (the special clothes, crowns, or symbols that show someone’s royal or official power), restitution (returning something to its original owner), reconcile (to make peace after conflict or disagreement). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Ghana received more than 130 gold and bronze artifacts from Britain and South Africa. These items were once part of the Asante Kingdom’s treasures . A long time ago, British soldiers stole some of these objects, while museums and collectors bought the others. The artifacts include royal objects, drums, and gold weights that show the culture and beliefs of the Asante people. During a ceremony in Kumasi, King Otumfuo Osei Tutu II thanked the South African company AngloGold Ashanti and British art expert Hermione Waterfield for giving the objects back. The return is an important step for Ghana, which wants to bring home its lost history. Difficult words: artifact (an old object, often found in museums), treasure (valuable things such as gold or jewels), collector (a person who gathers and keeps special objects). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Ghana gets back its old gold and bronze things from Britain and South Africa. People take these things from the Asante Kingdom many years ago. British soldiers steal some of them. Other things get to museums and collectors. The things are very old. They show the life and culture of the Asante people. There are gold weights , drums, and royal things. The king of the Asante people, Otumfuo Osei Tutu II, is very happy. He thanks a South African company and a British art expert. They help to give the things back. Now people in Ghana can see the things again in a museum. It is an important day for the country. Difficult words: collector (a person who gathers and keeps special objects), weight (a small object which people use to find out how heavy something is), royal (connected to a king, queen, or their family). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Uzbekistan opens a new educational center inside the Center of Islamic Civilization in Tashkent. The center allows children to explore the country’s rich heritage using technology, storytelling, and interactive experiences. Digital exhibits and animations show the lives of famous Central Asian scholars and scientists. Children can learn how science, art, and creativity shaped the Islamic world. The center also has the International School of Calligraphy, where artists teach both traditional and modern styles of writing. The library contains more than 35,000 books and 2,500 manuscripts . Through fun activities, interactive displays, and storytelling, children gain knowledge of Uzbekistan’s history while developing skills in creativity, learning, and cultural respect. They can use the space to understand history, build curiosity , and connect past knowledge with their own lives. By blending heritage with innovation, the center inspires young people to feel proud of their culture and values. This project shows how learning can be exciting, engaging, and meaningful for the next generation. Difficult words: manuscript (a handwritten book), curiosity (the desire to learn, know, or understand something), blend (to mix two or more things). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In Tashkent, Uzbekistan, a new center for children opens inside the Center of Islamic Civilization. Children can learn about the country’s history, famous scientists, and artists. The center uses digital exhibits, stories, and games to make learning fun. Children see animations about scholars and learn how they made important discoveries. There is also a school of calligraphy where artists teach beautiful writing. The library has more than 35,000 books and 2,500 old manuscripts . The center helps children understand the past and connect it with their lives today. By mixing tradition with new ideas, the center shows how learning can be exciting and meaningful for children. It helps them feel proud of Uzbekistan and its history. Difficult words: scholar (a person who studies a subject deeply and has much knowledge about it), calligraphy (art of beautiful writing), manuscript (a handwritten book). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In Tashkent, Uzbekistan, there is a new center for children. Children can learn about the country, history, and famous people. They play with digital games, watch animations, and hear stories. The center has a place to learn beautiful writing called calligraphy. Children can see many books in the library. They can learn about old scientists and artists. The center helps children know more about their country and feel proud . They can play, learn, and enjoy at the same time. Children can discover new things and connect the past with today. The center makes learning fun and interesting for every child. Difficult words: center (a place for learning), proud (when you feel pleased about something you or someone else does), connect (to join or link two things together). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Earthquakes, flooding, and hurricanes cause enormous damage to infrastructure and trap people inside collapsed buildings. A Belgium non-profit company APOPO is training rats to search the disaster zones for survivors. The rats wear high-tech backpacks that provide real-time wireless audio-visual communication with the company. The technology includes a video camera and audio which helps trainers work with the rat to find people. It also helps emergency workers communicate with the survivors. African giant pouch rats are curious and like to explore. They are very biddable , and they can be trained much like a dog. In addition to their adventurous spirit, their small size and excellent smell sense makes them perfect for locating things in tight space. The rats are being trained in a simulated disaster zone. They must locate the target person in an empty room, pull a switch on their vest to trigger a beeper, and then return to base for a reward. Trainers are gradually increasing the complexity of the environment to make it as close to reality as possible. Difficult words: real-time wireless audio-visual communication (communication with live audio and video and without wires), biddable (easily taught or controlled), complexity (many parts connected in a complicated way). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Trainers from Belgian company APOPO are training rats to search for people in disaster zones . Rats are very curious and they like to explore, so people train them just like dogs. They are very small, so they can easily move through debris . Also, they have very good smell to find things. The animals wear a small backpack with special technology. A video camera and a device helps rescuers communicate with survivors . Currently people train the rats in a simulated disaster zone. When the rat finds the person in an empty room, it pulls a switch on their vest. This sends a signal to rescuers that someone is in the debris. Then, the rat returns to the rescuers, and they reward the animal. Difficult words: disaster zone (an area where a disaster happens, for example, after an earthquake or flood), debris (broken pieces of buildings and other things), survivor (a person who lives after something very bad happens), simulated (something that looks real but it is not real). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Trainers train rats to look for people in disaster zones. A disaster zone is a place where something bad happens. It can be an earthquake, flood, or hurricane. Rats are small. They can easily move around the area. They have a very good sense of smell. People can train rats like dogs. Rats are very curious . They like to search through places. Trainers teach the rats in a place like a disaster zone. The place must look real. The rats wear a special bag. A video camera is in it. A communication device is in it, too. A person can talk to rescuers with the device. Difficult words: curious (interest to learn about people and things), communication (talk or write with other people), rescuer (a person who saves someone from a dangerous situation). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

FIFA, the world football governing body, is launching an annual Peace Prize, which will be awarded for the first time next month in Washington, DC. President Gianni Infantino explained that the prize will honor exceptional actions promoting peace, although he didn’t reveal the recipient. The award is part of FIFA’s Football for the World campaign, which emphasizes the role of football in bringing people together and giving hope. Infantino has a close relationship with US President Donald Trump, who recently failed to win the Nobel Peace Prize. Some observers speculate that Trump could receive FIFA’s new award, though the organization insists it cannot solve geopolitical problems. FIFA also maintains that sports and politics should remain separate, even if its actions suggest otherwise. The prize will be announced during the World Cup draw on December 5th in Washington, adding global attention to both football and peace initiatives, despite public amusement and mixed reactions from fans and commentators. Difficult words: speculate (to form opinions about something without having the necessary information or facts), geopolitical (relating to the politics of countries or regions), amusement (finding something funny or entertaining). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

FIFA will give a new Peace Prize every year. Somebody will get the first prize in Washington, DC, next month. FIFA’s president, Gianni Infantino, said the award will honor people who do special things to support peace. He didn’t say who would get the prize. This award is part of FIFA’s plan to show that football can bring people together and give hope. Infantino is a friend of US President Donald Trump, so some people think Trump might get the award because he wanted the Nobel Peace Prize. But FIFA says sports and politics should stay separate . The prize will be announced during the World Cup draw on December 5th. Many fans are amused , but some like the idea of connecting football with peace. Difficult words: honor (to show respect or recognition), separate (apart from each other), amused (finding something funny). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

FIFA will make a new Peace Prize. The first ceremony will happen in Washington, DC, next month. FIFA president Gianni Infantino says that the prize is for people who help peace . He does not say who will get it. Football can help people come together and feel hope. Infantino is a friend of US President Donald Trump. Some people think that Trump may get the prize. FIFA says football and politics are two different things. Somebody will get the prize at the World Cup draw on December 5th. Many people find this funny. Some people like the idea that football can help bring peace. The prize is new, and it shows that sports can try to do something good for the world. Difficult words: prize (something a person gets for a good action or winning), peace (a time without a war or conflict), draw (an event to decide something, like a game schedule). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Communities in Asia, Africa, and South America consider meal worms and crickets to be superfoods , and insects are a common part of their diet. Scientists discovered that mealworms can taste like meat when they’re cooked with sugar. Depending on how you cook them, their flavor changes. A steamed mealworm gives off a sweetcorn-like aroma ; however, if you roast or deep fry it, it tastes like shrimp. Experts say that insects are a great source of protein and other nutrients , and they are much better for the planet than the traditional meat diet. Insects use up less land and water, and they produce almost no greenhouse gas emissions. Difficult words: superfood (a food that’s considered to be especially beneficial for health), aroma (a pleasant smell), nutrient (a special ingredient in food or liquid we need for healthy growth and development). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In many parts of the world, people eat insects. They are a normal part of people’s diet because they are everywhere, and they are healthy to eat. In the Western World, many people think that eating insects is disgusting . Scientists said that meal worms tasted like meat, and they tasted differently if you cooked them differently. If you steam them, they smell like sweetcorn. If you roast or fry them, they taste like shrimp. Insects as food have more benefits. They are healthy and better for the planet than meat. They need less land and water, and they don’t make any gases like cows and other big animals. Difficult words: diet (food which someone usually eats), disgusting (something very unpleasant or something that tastes bad), mealworm (a bug baby, which destroys some foods). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Insects are very small animals. They can be spiders, bugs, or worms . In many parts of the world, people eat insects. It is a normal food for them to eat insects. Insects are very healthy. Many Westerners don’t like eating insects. They think that they are disgusting . Some insects taste like meat. For example, if you steam a mealworm , it smells like sweetcorn. If you fry it, it tastes like a shrimp. Insects for food are much better than meat. Insects need less land and water. Cows and other animals make gasses that can be bad. Insects make almost none. Difficult words: worm (a small animal which has a long, soft body, and no legs), disgusting (something that doesn’t taste good or something unpleasant), meal worm (an insect which destroys food). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A US judge has dismissed the criminal case against Boeing over two deadly crashes of its 737 Max 8 planes that killed 346 people. The decision came after a request from the Department of Justice (DOJ), which had earlier reached a 2021 deal with Boeing to avoid prosecution if the company improved safety and transparency. However, in 2024, the DOJ said Boeing violated that agreement. The judge harshly criticized the government’s move, saying it failed to bring accountability and ensure the safety of passengers. Both crashes were caused by a flawed flight control system design. Families of the victims and experts worry that Boeing will not face enough independent supervision, as the company will now choose its own safety consultant instead of an outside monitor . Critics fear this decision could risk public confidence in air travel safety. Difficult words: accountability (being responsible for your actions), flawed (having mistakes or weaknesses), monitor (a person or group that checks if rules are followed). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A US judge stopped a criminal case against Boeing after two plane crashes killed 346 people. The government asked for the case to end, even though Boeing already broke a deal made in 2021. The deal said Boeing had to be honest and safe to avoid punishment . The judge said the government failed to make Boeing take full responsibility for the deaths. Both crashes happened because of a problem in the planes’ control system. Boeing will now choose its own safety consultant , not an independent one. Families of victims think this is unfair and dangerous. They believe it will be harder to make sure Boeing follows safety rules in the future. Difficult words: punishment (something bad that happens to someone because they did something wrong), responsibility (duty to take care of something or someone), consultant (a person who gives expert advice). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A US judge says that Boeing will not go to court after two plane crashes. 346 people die in the crashes. The government asks to stop the case . The judge says that this is not good. People must be safe when they fly. The crashes happen because one part of the plane does not work well. Boeing makes a deal before, but does not follow it. Now the company can pick its own person to check safety . Families of the people who die are very sad and angry. They want the planes to be safe and the company to tell the truth. Difficult words: judge (a person who decides in a court), case (a legal situation in court), safety (being safe from danger or harm). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Nancy Pelosi, the first woman to become Speaker of the US House of Representatives, has announced she will retire from Congress after more than 35 years of service. In her farewell video, Pelosi reflected on her long political career and her deep connection to her home city, San Francisco. She celebrated the city’s creativity, resilience , and diversity, calling it the most beautiful place on Earth. During her 20 terms in Congress, Pelosi helped pass major laws, including the Affordable Care Act and measures to support clean energy and job creation. She thanked San Franciscans for trusting her and said representing them was her greatest honor. Pelosi urged citizens to continue defending democracy and to keep San Francisco a beacon of hope and progress for future generations. Difficult words: farewell (when you say goodbye to someone), resilience (the ability to recover from problems), beacon (a symbol that gives hope or guidance). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Nancy Pelosi, a famous American politician, said she will retire from Congress. She was the first woman to be Speaker of the House of Representatives. In her message, she spoke with love about San Francisco, her home city, and called it a place of beauty and creativity . She said she is proud of helping people get better healthcare and supporting clean energy. Pelosi thanked her voters for their trust and said it was an honor to speak for them in Washington. She also asked people to stay active in democracy and to protect freedom and peace. She said San Francisco must continue to be a strong example for others in the future. Difficult words: creativity (the ability to make or think of new and original ideas), trust (the belief that someone is honest and will do the right thing), honor (great respect or privilege). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Nancy Pelosi is a famous American politician. She says she will stop working in Congress. She is the first woman to be Speaker of the House of Representatives. She talks about her city, San Francisco. She says it is a happy and strong place. She thanks people for trusting her for many years. She says she is proud to help people get doctors and homes. She tells people to keep working for peace and freedom . She says San Francisco is full of good people and big dreams. She wants everyone to believe in the future and stay strong together. Difficult words: trust (to believe that someone is honest and will do the right thing), proud (feeling happy because you or someone you care about does something good), freedom (the right to live, speak, or do things without control from others). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The Grand Egyptian Museum has officially opened near the pyramids of Giza after 20 years of construction. It cost around one billion dollars, financed mostly through Japanese loans. The new museum, one of the world’s largest dedicated to a single civilization, houses tens of thousands of artifacts, including all the treasures of the ancient Pharaoh Tutankhamun, shown together for the first time. Presidents, prime ministers, and royalty attended the grand opening, which featured fireworks and drone shows lighting the night sky over Cairo. The Egyptian government hopes the museum will boost tourism and help the country’s struggling economy. Despite challenges such as the Arab Spring, the pandemic, and regional conflicts, Egypt finally celebrates a new chapter in its long history, aiming to attract millions of visitors in the coming years. Built close to the Great Pyramids, the museum symbolizes national pride and cultural heritage. Difficult words: artifact (an old object made by humans), heritage (traditions and culture from the past). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Egypt opened the Grand Egyptian Museum near the pyramids of Giza. It took 20 years to build and cost about one billion dollars, mostly paid with Japanese loans . The museum shows many ancient objects and the full collection of Pharaoh Tutankhamun’s treasures . Leaders and guests from many countries came to the opening, which had fireworks and drones in the sky. The government hopes the museum will help tourism and make more money for the economy. People in Cairo say it is a reason for pride and happiness. The museum is one of the biggest in the world and shows Egypt’s long history and culture. Difficult words: loan (money that someone borrows and must pay back later), ancient (very old), treasure (very valuable things such as gold, jewels, or other expensive objects). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The Grand Egyptian Museum is now open near the pyramids of Giza in Egypt. It is one of the biggest museums in the world. It shows many beautiful things from ancient Egypt. It takes twenty years to build and costs about one billion dollars. Egypt borrows a lot of money from Japan. Inside, visitors can see many old things, for example, all the famous gold objects from Pharaoh Tutankhamun’s tomb . The museum will bring more tourists to Egypt and help the country’s economy. During the opening, there are fireworks and lights in the sky. Many people come to celebrate this special moment for Egypt. Difficult words: ancient (very old), pharaoh (the king of old Egypt), tomb (a special place where important dead people stay). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Shein, the Chinese online shopping giant, has banned all sex dolls and stopped selling adult products after a major scandal in France. The issue began when French authorities discovered that the site was offering dolls with childlike appearances, which caused public outrage. France’s finance minister, Roland Lescure, warned that Shein could be banned from operating in France if it ever sold such products again. In response, Shein said it had punished the merchants involved and improved its system by adding more banned keywords to prevent similar violations. France’s child protection commissioner , Sarah El Haïry, stated that buying such dolls is unacceptable and can be linked to criminal behavior. Meanwhile, Shein is planning to open a new store in Paris, but small protests have already taken place outside the location. The company said it condemns these acts and is conducting an internal investigation.
